title: vibrantix-partner-portal's framework add/remove UI calls backend endpoints that do not exist, unlike the equivalent client-panel action
description: vibrantix-partner-portal/src/services/msspService.js addProjectFramework/removeProjectFramework call POST /mssp/clients/:id/projects/:projectId/frameworks and DELETE .../frameworks/:code. vibrantix-backend/src/modules/mssp/mssp.routes.js defines no such routes anywhere — the only server-side path for changing a project's framework allocation is POST /mssp/clients/:clientOrgId/requests (the subscription-request workflow), which is exactly what vibrantix-client-panel's msspService.js addProjectFramework/removeProjectFramework correctly calls via submitRequest(). This is a genuine, verified cross-service drift bug: the Partner Portal implementation predates or diverged from the request-workflow refactor and will 404 in production.
preconditions: A managed client with an active project
Partner Portal build pointed at the real vibrantix-backend
steps: In the Partner Portal, open a client's project and attempt to add a licensed framework
Attempt to remove an already-allocated framework from a project
Compare against the same action performed from vibrantix-client-panel's /mssp/clients/:id page
expectedResult: BUG (regression guard): both Partner Portal actions currently 404 against vibrantix-backend since no matching route exists; the client-panel equivalent succeeds by submitting a subscription request instead. This case should fail until Partner Portal's msspService is updated to call POST /mssp/clients/:clientOrgId/requests with type:"framework" like the client-panel does.

title: Replaying POST /mssp/clients with a completed Idempotency-Key never creates a second client organization
description: mssp.controller.js createClient (lines 116-117): existingOp?.status==="complete" short-circuits to `res.json({ success:true, replayed:true, data: existingOp.result })` before any provisioning logic runs.
preconditions: A prior successful POST /mssp/clients call with idempotency key K
steps: Repeat the identical POST /mssp/clients call with the same Idempotency-Key: K and the same body
expectedResult: Response has replayed:true and the original result payload (with no temporaryPassword, per MSSP-SEC-006); exactly one client Organization/MsspClientRelationship exists for that idempotency key, confirmed by re-listing /mssp/clients.

title: MSSP provider organizations and their owner invitations are always routed to MSSP_PORTAL_URL, never CLIENT_URL
description: tenant-provisioning.service.js portalUrlForOrganizationKind() and createOrganizationWithKeycloak/inviteOrgUser: kind='mssp_provider' must always resolve redirectUrl to MSSP_PORTAL_URL; kind='mssp_client'/'direct_customer' must always resolve to CLIENT_URL. A regression here would silently invite an MSSP owner to log into the wrong portal.
preconditions: CLIENT_URL and MSSP_PORTAL_URL configured to distinct values
steps: Create an organization with kind="mssp_provider" and invite its owner
expectedResult: createKeycloakOrg and inviteToOrganization are called with redirectUrl===MSSP_PORTAL_URL for the mssp_provider case, and redirectUrl===CLIENT_URL for the mssp_client case.

title: Resending a previously-expired invitation resets its status to "pending" and pushes expiresAt out by 7 days, on both the provider and platform-admin resend endpoints
description: mssp.controller.js resendInvitation (lines 483-516) and admin.controller.js resendInvitation (lines 136-177) share the same behavior: status is reset to "pending", expiresAt = now+7days, resendCount incremented, and a 60-second cooldown (lastSentAt) is enforced on both endpoints identically.
preconditions: An invitation whose status has flipped to "expired" (past its expiresAt)
steps: POST /mssp/invitations/:id/resend for a provider-facing expired invitation
POST /admin/tenant-management/invitations/:id/resend for a platform-admin-facing expired invitation
Immediately retry each resend a second time
expectedResult: Both first calls succeed, flipping status back to "pending" with a new 7-day expiresAt and resendCount+1. Both immediate second calls are rejected with a 60-second cooldown conflict.

title: A second invitation to the same email at the same target org is blocked while the first is still pending, but allowed once it is revoked
description: invitation.model.js's partial unique index { targetOrgId, email } with partialFilterExpression status:'pending' (lines 37-40) enforces exactly one live pending invite per (org,email) pair at the database layer, independent of any application-level duplicate check.
preconditions: A pending TenantInvitation for user@example.com at client org C
steps: Attempt to invite user@example.com to client org C again while the first invitation is still pending
Revoke the first invitation, then invite user@example.com to client org C once more
expectedResult: The first re-invite attempt fails (duplicate-key/conflict). After revocation, the second invite attempt succeeds and creates a new pending TenantInvitation.

title: Revoking a framework from a provider's licensed catalog does not retroactively touch any client project that already activated it
description: admin.controller.js replaceFrameworkCatalog only updates MsspFrameworkLicense rows (status->'revoked'); it never touches ClientFramework documents on already-provisioned client projects. The admin-panel UI itself documents this intent ('Changes restrict future allocation; existing paid client data remains preserved' — mssps/[providerId]/page.jsx). Regression risk: a future reconciliation job could incorrectly cascade a license revocation into client-level framework deactivation.
preconditions: Client project already has an active ClientFramework for SOC 2, provisioned while the provider was licensed for it
steps: Admin revokes SOC 2 from the provider's licensed catalog via replaceFrameworkCatalog
Reload that client project's framework list
expectedResult: The client project's existing SOC 2 ClientFramework record remains status="active" and fully functional; only new allocation attempts (resolveLicensedFrameworks) are blocked from selecting SOC 2 going forward.

title: Revoking an invitation that already granted project access releases the consumed user-seat quota for every affected project
description: tenant-provisioning.service.js removeInvitedUserProjectAccess() (lines 320-328) is called from both mssp.controller.js revokeInvitation and admin.controller.js revokeInvitation: it deletes the invited user's ProjectMember rows and releases the "users" quota consumed by inviteOrgUser for each of those projects — preventing a phantom seat that stays consumed forever.
preconditions: An invited-but-not-yet-accepted client user has ProjectMember rows on 2 projects, each consuming one "users" quota unit
steps: Revoke that pending invitation via DELETE /mssp/invitations/:id
Re-check each project's remaining users quota
expectedResult: Both projects' consumed "users" quota decreases by 1 (returning to its pre-invite level); the ProjectMember rows for the revoked user are deleted; the user's status becomes "removed".

title: A provider can never hold two active MsspFrameworkLicense rows for the same framework, even under concurrent catalog updates
description: mssp-framework-license.model.js: two compound unique indexes, { providerOrgId, frameworkId } and { providerOrgId, frameworkCode } (lines 23-24), guard against duplicate license rows regardless of application-level upsert logic in replaceFrameworkCatalog.
steps: Fire two concurrent PUT /admin/tenant-management/mssps/:providerId/frameworks requests that both include the same new framework code
expectedResult: Exactly one MsspFrameworkLicense document exists for that (providerOrgId, frameworkId) pair afterward; the database unique index prevents a duplicate even if the upsert race were lost.
